intent: A child reader/listener roughly ages 10-12 (upper elementary). Pilot default for child-oriented adaptations of canonical suengj.com articles (SUE-570, Post-V2 Pilot & Owner Adoption). Named explicitly because a vague '아동용' / 'child' audience is not a usable profile — vocabulary ceiling, concrete-vs-abstract reasoning, example choice, and attention span at this age differ from an adult beginner, not merely prior knowledge (contrast audience/beginner-learner.json, whose life_stage is not material).
domain_familiarity: No assumed exposure to the domain at all, including the general adult-world context an adult beginner would already have.
purpose: Wants to understand what is happening and why it is interesting or important, in terms that connect to things already familiar at this age.
assumed_knowledge: everyday concrete experience (school, family, games, animals, money as pocket-money-scale amounts)
no assumed adult-world context (workplaces, markets, institutions) unless it is explained from scratch
life_stage: child, roughly ages 10-12 (upper elementary) — this is one of the rare cases where life stage materially changes communication: vocabulary ceiling, concrete-vs-abstract reasoning, and attention span are all age-bound, not just prior knowledge.

text.explanation_depth: every term is either replaced with a plain-language equivalent or explicitly glossed on first use; no term is left unglossed on the assumption that context makes it clear
text.concreteness: concrete before abstract: ground every abstract idea in a specific, familiar example before naming the general principle
text.section_granularity: short conceptual steps; one new idea per step, each step short enough to hold in mind before the next

visual.abstraction: low; prefer literal, concrete depictions over symbolic or schematic encodings
visual.legend: the first-read relation must be understandable without reading a legend at all; a legend may exist as backup but cannot be load-bearing

audio.pace: slower than the beginner-learner adult pace
audio.useful_recurrence: higher than any other audience profile; restate the key idea in a second, differently-worded way before moving on

anti_patterns: Baby-talk: exaggerated simplicity, sing-song register, or vocabulary well below the stated reading level
Patronizing register: praising the reader for understanding, or narrating that a topic is 'hard' before explaining it
Cute analogies that distort the mechanism they stand in for, rather than genuinely modeling it
Lowering factual accuracy or dropping stated uncertainty in exchange for simplicity — simplifying the knowledge level must never simplify the truth (editorial/constitution.md §1-3)
